# ResumeProof Match: agent-readable product summary

Last updated: 2026-09-02
Canonical website: https://resumeproof.szw19990924.chatgpt.site/

## What ResumeProof Match is

ResumeProof Match is an evidence-first resume and job-description matching web application. It is designed for job seekers who want to decide whether a role is worth pursuing, understand which requirements their resume can prove, and improve wording without inventing experience.

The tool does not present keyword overlap as hiring probability. It separates three questions:

1. Role fit: whether the candidate's real experience covers the work and hard requirements.
2. Evidence coverage: whether the resume contains verifiable excerpts supporting those requirements.
3. Resume expression: whether supported experience is written clearly enough to be recognized.

## Supported inputs

- Resume or job-description text pasted into the browser.
- PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, PNG, JPG, JPEG, and WebP files up to the limit shown in the interface.
- Supported job-detail URLs. Some recruiting sites block reliable automated reading; when that happens, the tool asks the user to paste and review the complete JD instead of fabricating content.
- Images and scanned PDFs can use visual recognition when the deployment has OCR configured.

## Workflow

1. Add a base resume and a target job description.
2. Review the extracted text before analysis.
3. Run semantic analysis of requirements and resume evidence.
4. Inspect must-have, important, and bonus coverage, including the cited resume excerpts behind supported mappings.
5. Review proposed edits, their reasons, and any evidence warning.
6. Accept, reject, or edit each suggestion.
7. Review and approve the complete text draft.
8. Choose a resume layout and export HTML, PDF, or DOCX.

## Evidence rules

- Equivalent wording and transferable experience may support a requirement when a relevant resume excerpt exists.
- A partial signal is not treated as complete ownership or complete qualification.
- Missing evidence is shown as a gap.
- Rewriting can make supported experience easier to see; it cannot create tools, responsibilities, metrics, or outcomes the candidate did not have.
- The user must verify employers, job titles, dates, metrics, tools, and proper nouns before export.

## Privacy model

Regular PDF, DOCX, and text files are read in the browser where possible. Confirmed resume and JD text is sent to the configured semantic-analysis provider after the user starts analysis. Images and scanned PDFs may be sent to the configured vision provider for recognition.

The public deployment has no user account system for the matching workflow. Drafts are retained only in the current browser tab. Optional quality-improvement samples require an explicit opt-in, are automatically redacted, can be deleted by reference, and are retained for no more than 30 days. Automated redaction may not catch every identifier.

Basic product analytics excludes resume text, JD text, filenames, full job links, company names, and job titles. See the current privacy page for the complete policy: https://resumeproof.szw19990924.chatgpt.site/privacy

## Limitations

- AI analysis can misunderstand requirements, miss context, or suggest unsuitable wording.
- Match scores do not predict ATS decisions, interviews, or offers.
- Job-link extraction depends on the source site's public accessibility and can fail when content is gated, rendered differently, or protected from automated access.
- ResumeProof Match is not a recruiter and does not apply to jobs on the user's behalf.
